{
  "measurements": [
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 80.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of potential therapeutics that fail when tested in people after animal studies suggest they will be safe and effective",
      "compared": "animal studies vs human testing",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Even after animal studies suggest that a treatment will be safe and effective, more than 80% of potential therapeutics fail when tested in people."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 100.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of experimental treatments for ALS that had been shown to ameliorate disease in an animal model but failed in the clinic",
      "compared": "ALS animal models vs human clinical trials",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 12,
      "n_counts": "experimental treatments",
      "verbatim": "Over the past decade, about a dozen experimental treatments have made their way into human trials for ALS. All had been shown to ameliorate disease in an established animal model. All but one failed in the clinic"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "survival benefit",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "survival benefit of the one ALS experimental treatment that did not fail in the clinic",
      "compared": "ALS animal models vs human clinical trials",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 1,
      "n_counts": "experimental treatments",
      "verbatim": "All but one failed in the clinic, and the survival benefits of that one are marginal."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "beneficial effect",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "beneficial effect of many drugs in ALS TDI's mouse model, despite prior reports of disease slowing in the same model",
      "compared": "ALS TDI mouse model vs published mouse model results",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 100,
      "n_counts": "potential drugs",
      "verbatim": "Many of these drugs had been reported to slow down disease in that same mouse model; none was found to be beneficial in our experiments (see ‘Due diligence, overdue’)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 100.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of compounds that failed in clinical trials after being tested by ALS TDI in a mouse model",
      "compared": "ALS mouse model results vs human clinical trials",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 8,
      "n_counts": "compounds",
      "verbatim": "Eight of these compounds ultimately failed in clinical trials, which together involved thousands of people."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "variation",
      "value": 10.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "variation in average lifespan of SOD1 mice",
      "compared": "SOD1 mice lifespan",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 5500,
      "n_counts": "mice",
      "verbatim": "Almost 90% of the mice had an average lifespan of 134 days, give or take 10 days."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "variability",
      "value": 4.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "variability in survival due to gender differences in SOD1 mice",
      "compared": "male vs female SOD1 mice survival",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Male SOD1 mice show symptoms as much as a week before females and die about a week earlier. Given that a week is a 4% variability in survival, such differences could easily be misconstrued as a drug effect."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "survival extension",
      "value": 30.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "survival extension of SOD1 mice treated with lithium",
      "compared": "lithium treatment in SOD1 mice",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "This is exemplified by a study showing that lithium can boost survival of SOD1 mice by 30 days, an astoundingly long time8."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "survival extension",
      "value": 30.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "survival extension in people with ALS treated with lithium",
      "compared": "lithium treatment in people with ALS",
      "species": [
        "human"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "A small clinical trial showed that it also extended life in people with ALS8."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "failure rate",
      "value": 100.0,
      "unit": "percent",
      "measures": "share of phase III clinical trials for lithium in ALS that showed any therapeutic benefit",
      "compared": "lithium clinical trials vs ALS patient outcomes",
      "species": [
        "human"
      ],
      "n": 3,
      "n_counts": "phase III clinical trials",
      "verbatim": "None of the three trials showed any therapeutic benefit9–11."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost",
      "value": 100000000.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "total cost of three phase III clinical trials for lithium in ALS",
      "compared": "lithium clinical trials cost",
      "species": [
        "human"
      ],
      "n": 3,
      "n_counts": "phase III clinical trials",
      "verbatim": "These enrolled hundreds of patients with a total cost of well over US$100 million."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost",
      "value": 330000.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "estimated cost to characterize a single drug's potential to treat disease in humans",
      "compared": "preclinical characterization cost vs clinical trial cost",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 1,
      "n_counts": "drug",
      "verbatim": "An investment of $330,000 is necessary just to determine whether a single drug has reasonable potential to treat disease in humans."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost",
      "value": 30000.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "estimated cost to characterize the toxicity of a molecule and assess its pharmacokinetic properties",
      "compared": "preclinical characterization cost",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 1,
      "n_counts": "molecule",
      "verbatim": "We estimate that it takes about $30,000 and 6–9 months to characterize the toxicity of a molecule and assess whether enough reaches the relevant tissue and has a sufficient half life at the target to be potentially effective."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "cost",
      "value": 100000.0,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "estimated cost to test whether a drug can extend an animal's survival",
      "compared": "preclinical survival extension test cost",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": 1,
      "n_counts": "dose",
      "verbatim": "If those results are promising, then experiments to test whether a drug can extend an animal’s survival are warranted — this will cost about $100,000 per dose and take around 12 months."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "number of doses",
      "value": 3.0,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "number of doses of a molecule that should be tested to establish real drug responses and suggest reasonable dosing levels",
      "compared": "dosing levels for drug efficacy testing",
      "species": [
        "animal"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "At least three doses of the molecule should be tested; this will help to establish that any drug responses are real and suggest what a reasonable dosing level might be."
    }
  ],
  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study discusses the challenges and necessary improvements in preclinical animal research to better predict drug efficacy and safety in humans, using ALS as a case study.",
  "what_it_found": "A high percentage of potential therapeutics fail in human trials after showing promise in animal studies, often due to poorly designed preclinical experiments and inadequate characterization of animal models.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "Even after animal studies suggest that a treatment will be safe and effective, more than 80% of potential therapeutics fail when tested in people.",
      "topic": "High failure rate"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Animal models of disease are frequently condemned as poor predictors of whether an experimental drug can become an effective treatment.",
      "topic": "Poor predictors"
    },
    {
      "quote": "All had been shown to ameliorate disease in an established animal model. All but one failed in the clinic",
      "topic": "ALS trial failures"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Almost 90% of the mice had an average lifespan of 134 days, give or take 10 days.",
      "topic": "Mouse lifespan variation"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Given that a week is a 4% variability in survival, such differences could easily be misconstrued as a drug effect.",
      "topic": "Gender variability"
    },
    {
      "quote": "An investment of $330,000 is necessary just to determine whether a single drug has reasonable potential to treat disease in humans.",
      "topic": "Preclinical investment"
    }
  ]
}
